Paste the same block every time. Drift dies.

Brand drift in generated assets comes from re-describing the look each time. So don't. There is one Style Block below — it goes into every image prompt, unchanged. Then you add one line describing the subject. That's the whole system.

STEP 01

Paste the Style Block

Unchanged, every time, at the top. Never paraphrase it — paraphrasing is how drift starts.

STEP 02

Add one Subject line

Pick a recipe below and fill the {BRACKETS}. One sentence of subject is enough.

STEP 03

Append the Never list

The negative prompt does more work than the positive one. It kills the stock-photo look.

STEP 04

Keep the seed

When one comes out right, save the seed and reuse it for that asset class. Consistency beats novelty.

THE FRIED GUY RULE

Never generate him. He is existing artwork — composite the real file. If a prompt returns a cartoon electrocuted man, you have drifted. He only ever appears inside a hazard-stripe warning label, one per page, never on a money page or an estimate.

DRIFT CHECKLIST — RUN BEFORE ANYTHING SHIPS
Is there exactly one yellow?

One accent per image. Two yellows and it reads discount, not premium.

Would a real electrician wince?

Impossible wiring, backwards breakers, no PPE. Tradespeople are the audience.

Does it look like stock?

Crossed arms, white teeth, blue gradient. If it could sell insurance, kill it.

Is the purple ours?

#7B2FF7, not magenta, not indigo. Hold it against the truck photo.

Any invented text?

Never let a model render the logo, phone number, or license. Composite real type.

WHEN TO GENERATE AT ALL

Generated imagery is scaffolding, not the goal. Real panels, real crews and the real purple trucks outperform anything a model makes — a documentary photo of Grant beats a perfect render every time. Use these prompts for backgrounds, textures, and placeholders while you build the real photo library.
